result: Train 970 red explained and fixed: the hot-text regen read libc.a's section names with readelf -SW, which cuts at 256 bytes, so a traced 538-byte try_fold over a find_named closure was never listed; the names are now read whole (objdump -h), and regen fails on any traced library function whose section the listing missed
head: b7b37e33f

gate.affected: 669 passed / 0 failed (7 suites, direct tier, gate-honest-metrics-3-gate4)

informational: v0 key walker (keys.py and xtask/src/hottext.rs V0::decimal) reads a leading-zero run as one number, so names with nested closures (`000`) fall back to the plain strip; both sides agree and no list crosses a build (LT-5), so grouping is unaffected; recommend a small follow-up reading `0` as one digit, with a test
xtask/src/so.rs exclude_link_edges still reads section names with readelf -SW (cut at 256 bytes); not changed here
The merged train head b3f3fd771 was not rebuilt here (the brief allows no merge); the cause is the list step, which drops every traced function whose section name is over 256 bytes, on any head

impact.what: traced libc.a functions whose section names exceed 256 bytes now join the hot group (train 970: a locale per-directory try_fold ran outside it); on this branch's fast build 4 name-service functions (nss::passwd_cached, nscache::line_system x2, nscache::line) join
regen.sh fails by name on a traced library function whose section is missing from the section listing (was a silent drop)
xtask tests: keys.py --sections on a real archive with a 300-byte name and a non-ELF input; keys.py --unlisted; 4 plants CAUGHT
